concerns.text: The spec redefines the research question. The idea explicitly asks to investigate 'How does the granularity of semantic tokenization and the expressiveness of logical predicates... affect the trade-off'. The spec (US-3, FR-006, SC-001) only compares a single fixed symbolic implementation against a neural baseline. It drops the required 'granularity' and 'expressiveness' variables (the independent variables), turning a parametric study into a binary A/B test. This is a fundamental drift from the stated research question.

Under-reach on the 'granularity' variable. The idea requires investigating how 'granularity of semantic tokenization' affects performance. The spec (US-1, FR-002) mandates mapping to a 'fixed taxonomy' but does not specify the mechanism to vary this granularity (e.g., coarse vs. fine taxonomies) or the requirement to run the experiment across multiple granularity levels. Without this, the core research question cannot be answered.

Under-reach on the 'expressiveness' variable. The idea requires investigating 'expressiveness of logical predicates'. The spec (US-1, FR-003) defines a fixed set of predicates ('on_top_of', 'near', 'before') but does not require varying this set (e.g., adding spatial relations vs. temporal only) to measure the trade-off. The spec treats the predicate set as a constant rather than a variable to be swept.

The third edge case contains a copy-paste error and malformed logic: 'The system MUST record a warning log... (See US-3)'. The text inside the 'What happens when' block is a full requirement sentence rather than a scenario description, and it references a User Story in a way that breaks the Given/When/Then flow. This needs rewriting to match the standard edge case format.
